reply_text:
Let me run the candidates live on today's data so each example comes with its actual output.㊥ (gist) Six examples, each run live just now on this week's memories, are written up with their outputs in futon3c 1164232cd, `holes/labs/M-象-2000/DEMO-2026-10-14-what-the-flat-memory-cannot.md`. The flat store holds one current text per memory file; everything below needs either a past version, a time, a cross-project link, a consistency check, or a join to the conversation.

㊢ (1, what memory said on a day) On 09-24 memory knew Zai was out on its weekly limit. The five-hour window, the thing that bit on 10-11, entered memory on 10-12. `asof 2026-09-24` versus `asof 2026-10-14` shows the lesson postdating the incident. The flat store cannot show that.

㊢ (2, how a lesson evolved) `history zai window` gives 17 events across three memories in three projects over five weeks, including the 10-12 rewrite withdrawn and re-said four hours later. The flat store shows one file's final text.

㊢ (3, net change versus events) Over 10-11 to 10-14 six real facts were said and withdrawn inside the interval, among them "run at most 3 Zai seats at once" and this evening's "Joe is planning time to completion by usage window". The endpoint delta hides them and events-between shows them. That is the distinction Lean proved in E-cool-memories, and the checker accepted today's live delta.

㊢ (4, contradictions) 18 open conflicts between pairs of memories, each with both quotes checked verbatim. One pair is route-by-standing-principle against surfacing-reads-blocker-fields, where one note calls ruling-shaped blocker matching a defect and the other requires it. The flat store hands a session both.

㊢ (5, the same lesson twice) 21 relation edges, 8 across projects. The Zai lesson in home was found to refine the voxterm one, which is why they were merged on 10-12. Two notes on futon1b heap pressure from expensive reads sit in different projects, and they describe this morning's GC spiral on :7073.

㊢ (6, the conversation side) The 象 records answer "what did Joe ask that nobody answered" (one item today) and now carry the Facts section wired this afternoon, three facts in force about M-象-2000. The McCarthy checks pass five of six on this session.

㊟ (what none of it does yet) The two halves meet only in that Facts section. A memory version is not yet shown beside the turn whose session wrote it, the brief still counts bellback-closed asks as open, and the :7073 store that holds the 象 evidence rows stays in its GC spiral until you restart it.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: (store as a unit) `minus40-store.service` replaced the ad hoc scope at 17:40:50Z and answered health 18 s later. The JVM command line carries the 2 GB heap after the alias's 1 GB, so the override took. The follower, relate and fault loops kept running through the restart, and a fresh `net-changed` over 10-13 to 10-14 answers in 2.4 s. The unit file is kept in minus40 under `scripts/systemd/` with the outage written into the README.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: (brief for all seats) `brief-enabled.txt` now reads `all`, with the old one-seat list kept beside it. A dry run as claude-16 produced about 3,900 characters: open asks with no answer linked, then recently changed memory. One thing to watch: that list shows my own reply paragraphs from this morning as asks by claude-16, because marked agent replies are read as acts. Whether an agent's 🈸 should count as an open ask is a question for the brief's author, not a fault in it.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: (Facts in the resume brief) The section loads m40.py itself, so it shares minus40's store, ten-minute cache and true-at rule. It keeps facts true now whose text or memory id mentions the mission id or its excursions, newest first, up to 15. When the store is down it falls back to the cache on disk and says so; it never fails the brief. For M-象-2000 it finds three: read-the-clock, zai-five-hour-window and minus40-memory-store, in 1.0 s. Test added, five pass.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: (seen on the way) The scratch store holds minus40's own test projects, the corner-store bench and the hooktest memories, so a broad term like `minus40` matches them by id and fills the section with fixtures. I left that alone; cleaning test projects out of the store is minus40's call.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: (still open from this morning) The live futon1b on :7073 is still in its GC spiral, and that is the one restart I did not make, since it is the shared store and your call.
